recommendedTextbook.title: Junior English Project for Secondary Schools 3
recommendedTextbook.author: N. Grant, D. Olagoke, J. Southern

topics.topic: Complex Sentences: Main and Subordinate Clauses (Noun & Adjectival)
subtopics: Definition of a clause (group of words containing a finite verb)
Main / independent clauses vs subordinate / dependent clauses
Noun clauses (functions as subject, object of verb, object of preposition)
Adjectival clauses introduced by relative pronouns (who, whom, whose, which, that)
objectives: Distinguish main clauses from subordinate clauses in complex sentences
Identify grammatical functions of noun and adjectival clauses

topics.topic: Adverbial Clauses: Time, Condition, Reason, Manner & Concession
subtopics: Identification of subordinating conjunctions introducing adverbial clauses
Adverbial clause of time (when, while, since, before, after)
Adverbial clause of condition (if, unless, provided that) and concession (although, even though)
objectives: Classify adverbial clauses by type and state their grammatical functions
Write complex sentences incorporating adverbial clauses of condition and concession

topics.topic: Question Tags and Modal Auxiliaries in Spoken and Written Discourse
subtopics: Golden rule: positive statement takes negative tag, negative statement takes positive tag
Intonation in question tags (rising intonation for real questions, falling for confirmation)
Modal auxiliaries: can/could (ability), may/might (permission/possibility), must/ought to (obligation)
objectives: Append correct question tags to positive and negative statements
Use modal auxiliaries appropriately in formal requests and school rules

topics.topic: Formal Letter Writing: Applications and Official Petitions
subtopics: Layout of formal letters: two addresses (writer address top-right, recipient address left)
Date, formal salutation ('Dear Sir/Madam'), underlined title/subject heading
Formal body paragraphs (no slang, no contractions) and sign-off ('Yours faithfully' + signature + full name)
objectives: Format an official formal letter according to BECE/WAEC specifications
Draft a formal letter of application for secondary school scholarship or leave of absence

topics.topic: Speech Work: Consonant Clusters (Initial and Final Clusters)
subtopics: Definition of consonant clusters (two or more consonants pronounced without an intervening vowel)
Initial clusters: two-consonant (/pl/, /br/, /st/) and three-consonant (/spl/, /str/, /skr/)
Final clusters: /-kts/ (acts), /-lpt/ (helped), /-ndz/ (hands), avoiding vowel epenthesis
objectives: Articulate consonant clusters cleanly without inserting intrusive vowel sounds
Transcribe and pronounce words containing three-consonant clusters correctly

topics.topic: Argumentative Writing: Debate Format & Persuasive Techniques
subtopics: Structure of debate speeches: addressing the chairman, panel of judges, timekeeper, audience
Taking a clear stand (proposing or opposing the motion)
Marshaling logical arguments with empirical evidence and rhetorical questions
Topic: 'Boarding Schools Foster Independence Better than Day Schools in Nigeria'
objectives: Structure an argumentative debate presentation adhering to formal protocol
Refute opposing points with civil, evidence-based counter-arguments

subtopics: Evaluation on complex clauses, question tags, formal letters, and debates
BECE standardized past question drill
objectives: Assess pupil performance against BECE English Language criteria

topics.topic: Summary Writing: Differentiating Essential Facts from Illustrative Examples
subtopics: Meaning and significance of summary writing in secondary education
Steps in writing a summary: skimming, identifying thesis statement, deleting illustrations and repetitions
Drafting concise summary sentences in candidate's own words
objectives: Extract 3 core arguments from a 500-word reading passage
Express extracted points in complete, grammatically sound sentences without mindless copying

topics.topic: Vocabulary Development: Words Associated with Law and Governance in Nigeria
subtopics: Judicial vocabulary: judiciary, litigation, plaintiff, defendant, verdict, acquittal, bail, appeal
Legislative and executive terms: constitution, democracy, bill, enactment, gazette, ballot
Reading and contextual exercises on civic governance
objectives: Use legal and governance register terms correctly in sentences
Complete specialized cloze tests centered on Nigerian constitutional democracy

topics.topic: Literature in English: Dramatic Elements and Poetic Devices
subtopics: Features of drama: script, dialogue, stage directions, acts, scenes, dramatis personae
Dramatic terminology: protagonist, antagonist, conflict, climax, catastrophe, soliloquy
Poetic devices: hyperbole (deliberate exaggeration), euphemism (mild expression for harsh truth), oxymoron
objectives: Analyze dramatic conflict in an assigned African play text
Identify hyperbole and euphemism in poetry and everyday Nigerian speech

topics.topic: Direct and Indirect Speech II: Conversion of Questions and Commands
subtopics: Reporting yes/no questions using 'if' or 'whether'
Reporting wh- questions (who, what, where, when, why, how) maintaining subject-verb order
Reporting commands and requests using infinitive structures (e.g. 'He told him to leave')
objectives: Convert interrogative and imperative direct sentences into reported speech without question marks
Observe backshifting of auxiliary verbs and pronoun agreement

topics.topic: BECE Mock Examination Masterclass & Lexis Speed Drills
subtopics: Timed 80-question BECE English Studies paper 1 (Objective)
Paper 2: Continuous writing and summary writing moderation
objectives: Complete standardized BECE mock examination under timed conditions

subtopics: Terminal BECE examination administration and script moderation
objectives: Complete junior secondary English Studies graduation evaluation
